contact_state_from_wrench — DRIVE pegtactile op

• Data kinds: table × signal × signal × signal × signal × signal → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.contact_state_from_wrench(kp, F, M_g, g, tip, axis, f_air: 'float' = 0.05, tau: 'float' = 0.35, tol: 'float' = 8e-05, geometry: 'bool' = True, tol_l: 'float' = 5e-05) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import pegtactile; pegtactile.contact_state_from_wrench(kp, F, M_g, g, tip, axis, f_air: 'float' = 0.05, tau: 'float' = 0.35, tol: 'float' = 8e-05, geometry: 'bool' = True, tol_l: 'float' = 5e-05) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("contact_state_from_wrench"))

Usage

Contact wrench (F that the peg receives from the hole and M about the grasp point g, world frame) → contact state (rules, no learning).

For a single point contact, the moment about that point is 0 (no couple at a point). For each geometrically touchable candidate point c (contact_candidates), if the minimum of the normalised residual e(c) = |M_g − (c − g) × F| / (|F| r) is below tau it is one point (chamfer if at the tip edge with depth < W); if no candidate can explain it and there are valid candidates at both the tip and the body, two points; if |F| < f_air, no contact. With geometry, Whitney's geometry takes precedence: at tilt θ, if the tip is deeper than l₂(θ) − tol_l below the narrowest part, it must touch both sides (two points forced). At the wedging boundary θ = c/μ the edge of the tip's friction cone passes through the mouth contact point (slope of the line joining mouth and tip c/θ = μ), and the two-point wrench cannot be distinguished from "one point at the mouth" —— a blind spot inherent in wrench-only rules. Returns state (CONTACT_STATES), e_tip, e_mouth, where ("none" / "tip" / "mouth" / "tip+mouth" / "?"), c (point of contact, for one point), Fmag, depth, forced. Raises ValueError: vectors not finite 3-component, tau ≤ 0.
